subject.title: WhatsApp QR-unavailable/headless login needs phone-code fallback

question: Should WhatsApp phone-code login be exposed through the generic channel login contract and `openclaw channels login --phone-number`, or should the fallback stay behind a WhatsApp-owned login surface?
rationale: The requested fix spans a public CLI option, plugin/channel auth contract shape, Baileys pairing behavior, and persisted WhatsApp credential classification, which is an API/product boundary rather than a pure bug fix.

options.title: Accept Generic Phone-Number Login
options.body: Keep the typed generic login-method path, but require QR compatibility, Baileys timing proof, partial-credential cleanup, and live/upgrade validation before merge.

options.title: Keep It WhatsApp-Owned
options.body: Rework the fallback so phone-code login remains local to the WhatsApp plugin without expanding the generic channel-auth contract.

options.title: Pause Pending Live Dependency Proof
options.body: Keep this issue open and defer the public entrypoint until a maintainer accepts the Baileys pairing-code timing and reliability contract.

recommendation.title: Accept Generic Phone-Number Login
recommendation.body: Keep the typed generic login-method path, but require QR compatibility, Baileys timing proof, partial-credential cleanup, and live/upgrade validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses CLI, plugin SDK/channel API, and WhatsApp login ownership; current history shows steipete on the central generic surfaces and recent WhatsApp QR-login work.
